title: Semantics of First-Order Logic
main_topics: Truth Value of a FOL Formula
subtopics: vars function on terms and formulae
Value of a term ᾱ(t) in a structure and assignment
Truth value S, α ⊨ φ (inductive definition)

definitions.definition: A function α: X → D mapping variables to domain elements of structure S.
The element ᾱ(t) ∈ D computed inductively: ᾱ(x) = α(x), ᾱ(c) = cˢ, ᾱ(f(t₁,…,tₙ)) = fˢ(ᾱ(t₁),…,ᾱ(tₙ)).
S, α ⊨ φ defined inductively; for atomic P(t₁,…,tₙ): S, α ⊨ P(t₁,…,tₙ) iff Pˢ(ᾱ(t₁),…,ᾱ(tₙ)) = 1.
A formula φ is satisfiable if there exist a structure S and assignment α such that S, α ⊨ φ.
A formula φ is valid if for every structure S and assignment α, S, α ⊨ φ.

algorithms: Inductive definition of S, α ⊨ φ
formulas: S, α ⊨ ∀x.φ  iff  for all d ∈ D: S, α[x↦d] ⊨ φ
S, α ⊨ ∃x.φ  iff  there exists d ∈ D: S, α[x↦d] ⊨ φ
examples: Showing ∃x.P(x) is satisfiable but not valid
learning_objectives: Define and compute the value of a term in a structure and assignment.
Inductively evaluate the truth value of a FOL formula.
Determine satisfiability, validity, and equivalence of FOL formulae.
